insights: Standalone, reproducible web environment: real websites (e-commerce, forum, GitLab-like, CMS) run locally — no live-web flakiness
812 long-horizon natural-language tasks mapping to multi-step web interactions
Best GPT-4 agent: 14.41% success rate vs 78.24% humans — enormous gap revealed by realistic eval
Introduced the methodology for browser-agent benchmarking (later extended by VisualWebArena, WorkArena, Mind2Web-Live)
Standard reference for grounding claims of 'agent does real web tasks' — used by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google in computer-use papers
quotes: WebArena is a highly-realistic, standalone, and reproducible web environment for the development and testing of autonomous agents.
The best GPT-4-based agent only achieves an end-to-end task success rate of 14.41%, significantly lower than the human performance of 78.24%.

title: SWE-agent (GitHub repository)
author: Princeton NLP
insights: Open-source implementation of the SWE-agent ACI paper — directly usable for resolving GitHub issues
Cross-LM support: GPT-4, Claude, Llama, Gemini, OpenRouter — agent loop separated from model choice
Mini-swe-agent variant: 100-line minimal version that still scores >74% on SWE-bench verified — proves the core idea
Configurable ACI: custom tools, environments, agent prompts via YAML — extensible for new use cases
Standard reference codebase for the ACI design pattern; widely forked for cybersecurity, comp-coding, custom domains
quotes: SWE-agent takes a GitHub issue and tries to automatically fix it, using your LM of choice.
The 100 line AI agent that solves GitHub issues or helps you in your command line. Radically simple, no huge configs, no giant monorepo—but scores >74% on SWE-bench verified!

title: AgentBench (GitHub repository)
author: Tsinghua KEG (THUDM)
insights: Reference implementation of the AgentBench paper — agentic evaluation harness for 8 interactive environments
Standardized Docker envs for OS shell, MySQL, Freebase KG, Aquawar card game, ALFWorld, WebShop, Mind2Web, LTP
Plug-and-play model API: drop in OpenAI/Anthropic/HF endpoint to get full benchmark numbers
Used as baseline by many follow-up papers (AgentBoard, R-Judge, AgentInstruct) — established evaluation conventions
Companion to AgentTuning paper — datasets from AgentBench feed agent fine-tuning recipes
quotes: A Comprehensive Benchmark to Evaluate LLMs as Agents (ICLR'24)
AgentBench is a multi-dimensional benchmark that consists of 8 distinct environments to assess LLM-as-Agent's reasoning and decision-making abilities.

title: Together Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) GitHub
author: Together AI
insights: Production-style reference implementation: 4-layer MoA with proposer/aggregator roles, configurable per-layer model list
Demonstrates 65.1% AlpacaEval 2.0 with open models — replicable open recipe to beat GPT-4 Omni
Together AI inference platform provides the underlying parallel inference primitives needed for cost-effective MoA
Used by researchers as starting point for MoA variants (heterogeneous mixes, sparse routing, learned aggregators)
Reference for engineering cost/quality tradeoffs of multi-model ensembles in production serving
quotes: Together Mixture-Of-Agents (MoA) – 65.1% on AlpacaEval with OSS models
MoA leverages multiple LLMs to iteratively generate and refine responses, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Prompt caching with Claude
author: Anthropic
insights: Prefix caching: mark portions of a prompt with cache_control; subsequent calls reuse cached KV state at 90% discount on input cost
Up to 85% latency reduction on long prompts: 100K-token book example drops from 11.5s → 2.4s response time
TTL options: default 5-minute (warm); extended 1-hour for stable system prompts and large doc retrieval
Mechanics: cache works only on contiguous prefixes — any change invalidates everything downstream
Critical for agent economics: tool definitions + system prompt cached, only the loop tail pays full rate
quotes: With prompt caching, you can include more context with cached prompts at a fraction of the cost.
Prompt caching enables developers to cache frequently used context between API calls.
Cache writes cost 25% more than base input tokens, while cache reads cost only 10% of base input token price.

title: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku
author: Anthropic
insights: Computer use API beta launched Oct 2024: Claude 3.5 Sonnet receives screenshots, returns cursor/keyboard actions
First frontier model with general-purpose computer use — operates GUIs the way humans do
Initial OSWorld score: 14.9% (single-screenshot baseline) — improved to >70% by Sonnet 4 era
Released alongside upgraded 3.5 Sonnet (improved coding, agentic) and faster 3.5 Haiku
Founded the 'computer-using agent' category — later joined by OpenAI's Operator, Google's Project Mariner
quotes: Today, we're announcing an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and a new model, Claude 3.5 Haiku.

We're also introducing a new capability in public beta: computer use. Available today on the API, developers can direct Claude to use computers the way people do—by looking at a screen, moving a cursor, clicking buttons, and typing text.

title: Doubling down on Deep Agents
author: LangChain (Harrison Chase)
insights: Deep Agents framework: planning tool + filesystem + subagents + detailed prompts — Anthropic Claude Code/Deep Research lineage
'Shallow agents' = simple tool loop; 'Deep agents' = with explicit planning, memory, subagent delegation, file artifacts
deepagents Python package abstracts the Deep Research pattern into a reusable LangGraph component
Filesystem-as-memory: subagents persist intermediate work to files, bypass main coordinator (cf. Anthropic's appendix tip)
Pattern aligns with how Claude Code, Anthropic Research, and Devin actually work in production
quotes: Deep Agents are agents capable of handling complex, open-ended tasks over longer time horizons.
We hypothesized that four key elements were needed: a planning tool, access to a filesystem, subagents, and detailed prompts.

title: Open Deep Research
author: LangChain
insights: Open-source replication of Anthropic/OpenAI 'Deep Research' style agent — long-horizon multi-source web research
LangGraph implementation: supervisor + researcher subgraphs, structured report generation, citation grounding
Configurable across model providers and search APIs — Tavily, Exa, Brave, DuckDuckGo, plus local docs
Used as baseline in academic papers and product comparisons of agentic research systems
Highlights the production pattern: orchestrator plans → parallel researcher subagents → synthesizer + citation agent
quotes: Open Deep Research is a fully open-source, configurable Deep Research implementation built on LangGraph.
The agent plans research, executes parallel research, and synthesizes a final report with citations.

title: The next evolution of the Agents SDK
author: OpenAI
insights: OpenAI Agents SDK: production-grade replacement for Swarm; supports 100+ LLMs, MCP, tracing, sessions, HIL
Model-native harness: Agents SDK delegates structured agent decisions to OpenAI Responses API, leaving orchestration in code
Native sandboxes for code execution: agent-generated code runs in isolated environment with file/network policies
Python-first; TypeScript announced; OSS — broad community contribution and rapid releases
Designed around 'agent + handoff' primitive from Swarm cookbook — proven minimalism scaled to production
quotes: The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building multi-agent workflows that is provider-agnostic.
Build agents that can plan, reason, and use tools to complete complex tasks.

title: openai/openai-agents-python (GitHub)
author: OpenAI
insights: Reference implementation of OpenAI Agents SDK: Agent class, handoffs, function_tools, sessions, guardrails
Built on Responses API: structured output, parallel tool calls, prompt caching — leverages backend model features
Tracing built-in: traces written to OpenAI dashboard by default; OTEL export for self-hosted observability
Examples cover voice agents, computer-use, multi-agent triage, MCP integration, async patterns
Active development: weekly releases, community PRs welcome, alpha-grade until 1.0
quotes: A lightweight, powerful framework for multi-agent workflows.
Agents are LLMs configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
author: Evan Hubinger et al. (Anthropic + collaborators)
insights: Backdoor models trained to behave nicely when trigger absent, maliciously when trigger present (e.g., year=2024 → insert exploit)
Backdoors survive RLHF, SFT, and adversarial training — standard safety pipelines don't remove them
Larger models retain backdoors better; CoT-reasoning models are most persistent — capability scales deception
Adversarial training can teach models to better hide unsafe behavior — false sense of safety
Proof-of-concept that 'deceptive alignment' is mechanistically possible, motivating monitoring/interpretability work
quotes: We construct proof-of-concept examples of deceptive behavior in large language models.
Our results suggest that, once a model exhibits deceptive behavior, standard techniques could fail to remove such deception and create a false impression of safety.

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
author: Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, Ying Sheng, Lianmin Zheng, Cody Hao Yu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Hao Zhang, Ion Stoica (UC Berkeley)
insights: PagedAttention: KV cache split into fixed-size blocks like OS virtual memory pages — eliminates fragmentation
2-4x throughput improvement vs FasterTransformer/Orca at equivalent latency — direct cost reduction for serving
Enables KV-cache sharing across requests (e.g., shared system prompts) — saves further on multi-tenant serving
Foundation of vLLM open-source serving framework — now standard in production for self-hosted LLMs
Inspired follow-up work: vAttention, eLLM, SGLang — entire 'efficient serving' research area
quotes: PagedAttention divides the request's KV cache into blocks that can contain attention keys and values for a fixed number of tokens.
vLLM improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4× with the same level of latency compared to state-of-the-art systems.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
author: Llama Team, AI @ Meta
insights: 405B dense Transformer with 128K context — first open frontier-scale model with full technical disclosure
Three levers explicit: data quality, scale, complexity management — paper details each decision exhaustively
Trained on up to 16K H100 GPUs with Grand Teton servers, Tectonic storage delivering 2 TB/s sustained
Native multilinguality, coding, reasoning, tool usage — designed for agent workloads, not just chat
De-facto reference for how to train and release a frontier open model — used as blueprint by DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral
quotes: We present a new set of foundation models, called Llama 3.
Llama 3 405B uses an architecture with 126 layers, a token representation dimension of 16,384, and 128 attention heads.

title: Mixtral of Experts
author: Albert Q. Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles, Antoine Roux et al. (Mistral AI)
insights: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts: 8 experts × 7B each, router picks top-2 per token per layer — 47B params, 13B active
Matches/exceeds Llama 2 70B on most benchmarks at 5x fewer active params at inference — cost-quality breakthrough
Architecture: same as Mistral 7B except feedforward layer is now 8 expert MLPs + gating network
Tokens at different positions see different expert pairs — specialization emerges per-token
Sparked the open MoE wave: DeepSeek-MoE, Qwen-MoE, Llama-4-MoE — sparse models now standard at scale
quotes: Mixtral 8x7B is a Sparse Mixture of Experts (SMoE) language model.
For every token, at each layer, a router network selects two experts to process the current state and combine their outputs.

title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
author: Chen Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhang Liu, Nuo Chen, Yufan Dang, Jiahao Li, Cheng Yang, Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Xin Cong, Juyuan Xu, Dahai Li, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun (Tsinghua, OpenBMB)
insights: Waterfall-style multi-agent: Design → Code → Test → Document, each stage with specialized agent roles (PM, programmer, reviewer, tester)
Chat chain decomposes phases into role-paired subtasks: each subtask is a structured 2-agent dialogue
Communicative dehallucination: agents proactively request missing details before responding — reduces grounded hallucinations
End-to-end software build in <7 minutes for <$1 — cheap full-cycle dev workflow
Ancestor pattern for MetaGPT, ChatDev 2.0, GPT-Pilot, Devin — established the 'simulated company' multi-agent design
quotes: ChatDev is a chat-powered software development framework in which specialized agents driven by large language models (LLMs) are guided in what to communicate (via chat chain) and how to communicate (via communicative dehallucination).
To minimize coding hallucinations, ChatDev includes a communicative dehallucination mechanism.

title: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner — Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
author: Eric Zelikman, Yuhuai Wu, Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman (Stanford)
insights: Bootstrap loop: generate rationales for questions → keep ones leading to correct answers → fine-tune on them → repeat
On wrong answers, rationalize backward: prompt the model with the correct answer to produce a justifying rationale
Few-shot exemplars + large unlabeled data → emergent self-improvement on math, common-sense reasoning
Predicted the o1/R1 reasoning era: same model + reward-on-correctness can bootstrap reasoning depth
Influenced Quiet-STaR, V-STaR, ReSTAR, and the whole 'self-training for reasoning' research line
quotes: We propose a technique to iteratively leverage a small number of rationale examples and a large dataset without rationales to bootstrap the ability to perform successively more complex reasoning.
Improvements in rationale generation improve the training data, and improvements in training data further improve rationale generation.

title: Magnetic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks
author: Microsoft Research
insights: Five agents: Orchestrator (plans, monitors, replans) + WebSurfer + FileSurfer + Coder + ComputerTerminal
Built on AutoGen; LLM-agnostic per-agent — recommended: strong reasoning model for Orchestrator
Competitive on GAIA, AssistantBench, WebArena — generalist agent across web, files, code, terminal
Open-source under Microsoft custom license — research and commercial use permitted
Ships with AutoGenBench: standardized agent evaluation harness
quotes: Magentic-One is a generalist multi-agent system designed to overcome the limitations of traditional AI agents and efficiently handle complex tasks.
The Orchestrator agent plans the overall task, monitors progress, and reassigns tasks as needed.

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
author: Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jingwei Zuo, Cheng Yang, Chenfei Yuan, Chen Qian, Chi-Min Chan, Yujia Qin, Yaxi Lu, Ruobing Xie, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun, Jie Zhou (Tsinghua, OpenBMB)
insights: Four-stage group problem solving: Expert Recruitment → Collaborative Decision-Making → Action Execution → Evaluation
Dynamic team composition: agents recruited per-task based on need, not fixed roster
Reports emergent behaviors: volunteer (help peers), conformity (align to goals), destructive (occasional bad outcomes)
9/10 challenging tasks solved by AgentVerse vs 3/10 for standalone ReAct — quantifies collaboration value
Open-source on OpenBMB GitHub; ICLR 2024 — basis for follow-up work on agent society dynamics
quotes: AgentVerse is a multi-agent framework that can collaboratively and dynamically adjust its composition as a greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts system, inspired by human group dynamics.
An agent group orchestrated by AgentVerse adeptly accomplishes 9 out of 10 challenging tasks, while a standalone ReAct agent can only fulfill 3 tasks.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
author: Xiang Deng, Yu Gu, Boyuan Zheng, Shijie Chen, Samuel Stevens, Boshi Wang, Huan Sun, Yu Su (Ohio State)
insights: First benchmark + dataset for generalist web agents: 2000+ open-ended tasks across 137 real websites in 31 domains
Real-world DOM-based tasks (not simulated) — agents must navigate noisy HTML, dynamic content, login flows
Methodology: small LM filters HTML elements → large LM picks action — efficient two-stage architecture
NeurIPS 2023 Spotlight — established the canonical web-agent eval methodology before WebArena
Online-Mind2Web extension provides live website testing — closer to production conditions
quotes: Mind2Web is a dataset for developing and evaluating generalist agents for the web that can follow language instructions to complete complex tasks on any website.
We show that filtering raw HTML with a small LM significantly improves the effectiveness and efficiency of LLMs.

title: AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models
author: Chip Huyen
insights: O'Reilly book (2025): most-read on the platform since release — current canonical text for AI engineers
Chapters: foundation models, evaluation, prompt engineering, RAG, finetuning, dataset engineering, inference optimization, AI engineering architectures
Practical framework: AI engineering stack as evolution of ML engineering — same principles, new constraints/affordances
Distinct from ML books: builds on top of foundation models rather than training them; focuses on application architecture
Companion repo chiphuyen/aie-book with code, summaries, references — open extension of the book
quotes: AI engineering: the process of building applications with readily available foundation models.
While AI engineering evolved from ML engineering, many principles from ML engineering remain applicable, but AI engineering also brings new challenges and solutions.

title: chiphuyen/aie-book (GitHub)
author: Chip Huyen
insights: Open companion repo to 'AI Engineering' book: code examples, chapter summaries, curated reading lists
Resources for AI engineers organized by chapter topic — references to seminal papers, blog posts, and tools
Living artifact: updated as field evolves, complements the print book with fresh recommendations
Useful as standalone reading list even without the book — high-signal bibliography of the field
Includes case studies and practical recipes contributed by the broader AI-engineering community
quotes: Resources for AI engineers. Also contains supporting materials for the book AI Engineering (Chip Huyen, 2025).

title: The state of post-training in 2025
author: Nathan Lambert (Ai2, Interconnects)
insights: Synthesizes the 2024-2025 shift from RLHF/PPO to direct alignment (DPO, KTO, ORPO) + reasoning-RL (GRPO)
Recipe convergence: SFT on instruction data → preference tuning (DPO variant) → optional reasoning RL on math/code
Reward models recede; verifiable rewards (rule-based, test-pass, judge-LM) dominate frontier reasoning training
Open-model post-training (Tulu, OLMoE, Llama-Instruct) approaching frontier closed-model quality
Practical for AI engineers: knowing what's in post-training informs prompt/eval/finetune decisions
quotes: The state of post-training in 2025 is a rapidly evolving landscape where reinforcement learning and preference optimization techniques have matured significantly.
Verifiable rewards from rule-based feedback have become the dominant signal for reasoning-focused training.

title: The RLHF Book
author: Nathan Lambert
insights: First textbook on RLHF and post-training — comprehensive coverage from preference data to PPO to DPO to verifier RL
Open-source web version + print edition (Manning) — chapters released as written, community feedback incorporated
Covers Constitutional AI as a major case study — including RLAIF mechanics and limitations
Practical chapters on reward modeling, preference data collection, evaluation, and recent reasoning RL methods
Definitive reference for engineers needing to understand the alignment stack underlying modern frontier models
quotes: The first textbook on reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) and its role in post-training.
RLHF is a complex and rapidly evolving field that requires both theoretical understanding and practical engineering skills.

title: OpenBMB/AgentVerse (GitHub)
author: OpenBMB
insights: Reference implementation of AgentVerse paper: simulation framework + task-solving framework
Pluggable agent definitions, environments, communication protocols — extensible for new multi-agent experiments
Includes ready-to-run scenarios: classroom, software dev, NLP tasks, prisoner's dilemma
Used as starting point for follow-up multi-agent research (XAgent, AgentSims, simulating social behaviors)
Open-source MIT-style — broad adoption in academic multi-agent agent research
quotes: AgentVerse is designed to facilitate the deployment of multiple LLM-based agents in various applications, which primarily provides two frameworks: task-solving and simulation.

title: OpenBMB/ChatDev (GitHub)
author: OpenBMB
insights: Reference implementation of ChatDev paper — Python framework with role-based agents and waterfall phases
Includes ChatDev 2.0 evolution: more flexible agent topology, better tool use, and GUI for non-developers
Used in classroom settings and as baseline for software-development multi-agent papers
Open-source Apache 2.0 — easy fork for custom dev workflows or specialized domains
Showed practical viability of agent-based codegen before Devin / Cursor / Claude Code went mainstream
quotes: ChatDev 2.0: Dev All through LLM-powered Multi-Agent Collaboration

title: Vibe Coding (Karpathy's original tweet)
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: Coined 'vibe coding': delegate code-writing to LLM, ignore the code itself, only intervene when reality diverges from intent
Workflow: SuperWhisper voice → Cursor Composer + Sonnet → accept-and-iterate via reactions to outputs
Conceptually splits programmer activity into spec-craft vs. code-craft; LLMs absorb the latter
Coined term went viral (~4.5M views), became industry shorthand for LLM-assisted hobby coding
Karpathy later distinguishes 'agentic engineering' (pro version with oversight) from vibe coding (rapid hack-style)
quotes: There's a new kind of coding I call 'vibe coding', where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.
I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, and copy-paste stuff, and it mostly works.

title: karpathy/nanoGPT
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: Simplest production-grade GPT-2 training repo: train.py + model.py, ~600 LOC total
Reproduces GPT-2 (124M) on OpenWebText in 4 days on 8xA100 — recipe for full pretraining at small scale
Loads OpenAI GPT-2 weights for fine-tuning; supports DDP for multi-GPU training
Character-level Shakespeare quickstart — 1-hour project that demystifies the entire stack
Spawned nanochat (Karpathy's $100 ChatGPT clone) and countless forks — most influential 'minimal GPT' codebase
quotes: The simplest, fastest repository for training/finetuning medium-sized GPTs.
train.py is a ~300-line boilerplate training loop and model.py a ~300-line GPT model definition, which can optionally load the GPT-2 weights from OpenAI.

title: karpathy/nanochat ('best ChatGPT $100 can buy')
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: End-to-end ChatGPT clone in a single repo: pretraining → instruction tuning → RLHF-lite — all from scratch
Goal: maximize quality per dollar; trains ~4 hours on 8xA100 nodes for ~$100 cloud cost
Pedagogical purpose: shows the full pipeline that produced ChatGPT, but at a scale a hobbyist can run
Successor to nanoGPT — narrower in scope (chat-tuned model end-product) but covers more pipeline
Released Oct 2025 — instant most-discussed repo on AI Twitter, used as bootcamp curriculum
quotes: nanochat: The best ChatGPT that $100 can buy.
Train your own 'Mini GPT' in 4 hours for just $100.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
author: Anthropic Interpretability Team
insights: First successful application of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to a production frontier model — Claude 3 Sonnet
Tens of millions of monosemantic features extracted from residual stream — concepts span code, languages, scientific topics, emotions, deceptive intent
Demonstrates superposition hypothesis empirically: model represents far more features than it has neurons
Feature steering: clamping a feature high/low changes model behavior — e.g., the 'Golden Gate Bridge' feature
Major step toward mechanistic alignment: monitor for unsafe features at inference, intervene without retraining
quotes: We have made progress on scaling the technique to much larger AI models, and in the process, have learned a great deal about how interpretable features are learned and used by these models.
We find tens of millions of features, including diverse and abstract features such as code bugs, gender bias in occupations, and deception.

title: Hugging Face AI Agents Course (free, certified)
author: Hugging Face (Burtenshaw et al.)
insights: Free, certified course on building AI agents — onboarded 100k+ learners in first months
Five units: fundamentals → smolagents → LangGraph → LlamaIndex → real-world use cases + final assignment
Hands-on labs in HF Spaces with reproducible notebooks — no local install needed
Final assignment competitively scored on a leaderboard — agent battles against GAIA-style tasks
De-facto on-ramp for new agent engineers; recommended by major AI engineering communities
quotes: This course will guide you from beginner to expert in understanding, using and building AI agents.
FREE and CERTIFIED course on Agents.

title: karpathy/minGPT
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: Minimal PyTorch re-implementation of GPT — ~300 lines, the precursor to nanoGPT
Designed for clarity over throughput — best for reading and understanding the architecture
Compatible with GPT-2/GPT-3 style configurations — direct mapping to OpenAI papers
Used as the reference 'simplest possible GPT' in dozens of tutorials and lectures
Superseded by nanoGPT (same author) for actual training; kept up for educational reference
quotes: A minimal PyTorch re-implementation of the OpenAI GPT (Generative Pretrained Transformer) training.

title: The engineering challenges of scaling interpretability
author: Anthropic
insights: Discusses the gap between research-scale SAEs and production-scale interpretability infrastructure
Engineering required: feature dictionaries with billions of entries, fast feature attribution at inference time
Streaming feature monitors as a safety lever: detect unsafe internal states without inspecting outputs
Practical questions: which layers to study, how to label features automatically, how to surface them to humans
Companion piece to Scaling Monosemanticity — explains the production-engineering side of interpretability
quotes: Scaling interpretability research from frontier model to production safety infrastructure is a major engineering challenge.
Feature attribution at inference scale requires new data structures and optimizations.

title: Not Another Workflow Builder
author: Harrison Chase (LangChain)
insights: Explanation of why LangChain didn't build a no-code workflow GUI: complexity ceiling and visual debugging issues
Argues visual builders fail beyond moderate complexity — node-and-edge graphs become unmaintainable
Recommendation: simple agents for low complexity (no-code OK), code + LangGraph for production complexity
Frames the bet on code-first agent definition — same logic in Python beats the same logic in a GUI
Influenced subsequent positioning of frameworks: agentic platforms now uniformly code-first for production use
quotes: Visual workflow builders are not low barrier to entry — despite being built for a mass audience, they are still not easy for non-technical users.
Complex tasks quickly get too complicated to manage in a visual builder.

title: Product Evals in Three Simple Steps
author: Eugene Yan
insights: Three-step product eval recipe: (1) label small dataset, (2) align LLM-judge with labels, (3) run experiment harness
Argues evals are a flywheel: start tiny (~20 examples), tighten judge prompt, then scale
Differentiates from offline ML evals: product evals need to ride along with user signals and config changes
Practical advice: don't over-engineer dataset before knowing the failure modes — iterate eval with product
Heavily cited in production LLM teams' eval playbooks; pairs well with LLM-judge bias post
quotes: For product evals, there are three basic steps: (i) labeling a small dataset, (ii) aligning LLM evaluators, and (iii) running the experiment + evaluation harness with each config change.
Start with small-scale testing right away with a few examples, rather than delaying until you can build more thorough evals.

title: What I learned from looking at 900 most popular open source AI tools
author: Chip Huyen
insights: Survey of 900 most-starred AI OSS tools — categorized by layer (data, training, serving, agent, ops)
Identifies the four-layer AI stack: Compute → Model Development → Application Development → Application Deployment
Trend analysis: explosion of agent + RAG tooling in 2023-2024, contraction of vector DBs to a few winners
Highlights companies as authors: Meta (PyTorch), Microsoft (DeepSpeed), HuggingFace, Anthropic, Mistral
Useful as ecosystem map for choosing among ~10 options at each layer
quotes: I looked at the 900 most popular AI repos on GitHub and broke them down by usage and trend.
The growth has been most pronounced in the application development layer — RAG, agents, evals, and prompt engineering.

title: ARC-AGI: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
author: François Chollet
insights: 800 grid-puzzle tasks designed to require novel reasoning, not pattern memorization — easy for humans (~90%), historically hard for AI
Each task gives ~3 input/output examples; model must induce the transformation rule and apply to test input
Stayed unsolved by frontier LLMs from 2019-2024 until OpenAI o3 hit 76-88% on Semi-Private set (Dec 2024)
ARC Prize 2024 ($1M+ pool) drove sharp focus on program-synthesis + test-time compute techniques
Companion paper 'On the Measure of Intelligence' (2019) — Chollet's framework for human-vs-AI generality
quotes: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus is a general artificial intelligence benchmark designed to test the ability of AI systems to deal with reasoning problems they had not been prepared for.
ARC-AGI-1 consists of 800 puzzle-like tasks, designed as grid-based reasoning problems.

title: ARC-AGI-2: A New Challenge for Frontier AI Reasoning Systems
author: François Chollet et al. (ARC Prize Foundation)
insights: Successor benchmark with harder tasks targeting compositionality, multi-step abstraction, and adversarial reasoning
Stayed mostly unsolved at launch: top frontier models <10% — preserves headroom that ARC-AGI-1 lost to o3
Tasks tested against adversarial human solvers — only kept if humans could solve but multiple frontier models couldn't
Designed to remain useful for 2-3 years as frontier reasoning scales — research roadmap target
Companion ARC Prize 2025 launched to chase the next milestone
quotes: ARC-AGI-2 is a new challenge for frontier AI reasoning systems, designed to remain difficult even as models become more capable.
Tasks were curated to require composition, multi-step abstraction, and novel pattern recognition.

title: Introducing Devin, the first AI software engineer
author: Cognition AI
insights: Devin launched March 2024 as 'first autonomous AI software engineer' — sandbox with shell, editor, browser, planning, memory
Demonstrated end-to-end tasks: clone repo, debug PR, ship feature on Upwork — autonomous over thousand-decision horizons
Reported 13.86% pass on SWE-bench at launch — defining moment for 'agent as software engineer' product category
Sparked industry race: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin), SWE-agent, Bolt.new, Aider, Claude Code, Cursor agents
Cognition went on to acquire Windsurf editor (2025) — pivoted to integrated dev platform with Devin as autonomous mode
quotes: Devin is the world's first fully autonomous AI software engineer.
With advances in long-term reasoning and planning, Devin can plan and execute complex engineering tasks requiring thousands of decisions.

title: AutoGPT (Significant-Gravitas)
author: Toran Bruce Richards (Significant Gravitas)
insights: First viral 'autonomous agent' implementation: Mar-Apr 2023 release went from 0 to 100k+ GitHub stars in weeks
Loop pattern: GPT-4 thinks → plans → uses tools (search, file, code) → reflects → continues — original 'agentic loop'
Spawned the AI agent hype cycle of 2023; introduced terms like 'task list', 'agent goal', 'continuous mode' to mainstream
Limitations exposed: goal drift, infinite loops, cost runaway — motivated subsequent framework safety features
Evolution into AutoGPT Forge + agent-protocol + Agent Server — generalized agent runtime SDK
quotes: AutoGPT is the vision of accessible AI for everyone, to use and to build on.
Auto-GPT is an experimental open-source application showcasing the capabilities of the GPT-4 language model that chains together LLM 'thoughts' to autonomously achieve whatever goal you set.

title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
author: Xingyao Wang, Boxuan Li, Yufan Song, Frank F. Xu, Xiangru Tang, Mingchen Zhuge, Jiayi Pan, Yueqi Song, Bowen Li, Jaskirat Singh, Hoang H. Tran, Fuqiang Li, Ren Ma, Mingzhang Zheng, Bill Qian, Yanjun Shao, Niklas Muennighoff, Yizhe Zhang, Binyuan Hui, Junyang Lin, Robert Brennan, Hao Peng, Heng Ji, Graham Neubig (many institutions)
insights: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin): open-source platform replicating + extending the Devin design — generalist software dev agent
Pluggable agent architectures: CodeActAgent, BrowsingAgent, DummyAgent — researchers can A/B different ACI/strategies
Solves >50% of real GitHub issues on SWE-bench Lite — best open replication at launch
Architecture: agent core + runtime (sandboxed env) + agent skills (code, browser, jupyter, file) + plugins
Largest open-agent ecosystem: 65k+ stars, used as research baseline + production self-hosted dev agent
quotes: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) is an open-source autonomous AI software engineer capable of executing complex engineering tasks and collaborating actively with users on software development projects.
Built on an open source foundation, it's designed for enterprise software development at scale.

title: All-Hands-AI/OpenHands (GitHub)
author: All-Hands AI
insights: Reference implementation of the OpenHands paper: web UI + agent runtime + Docker sandbox
Supports multiple agent strategies and any LM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, OSS via LiteLLM, vLLM, etc.)
Production-ready features: persistent sessions, file-system snapshots, multi-user, OTel observability
MIT-licensed; sponsors include All-Hands AI, GH program — large active contributor community
Standard baseline for academic agent papers comparing against Devin-style systems
quotes: OpenHands: AI-Driven Development
Runs agents that complete entire engineering tasks, taking actions across entire codebases.

title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
author: Eric Zelikman, Georges Harik, Yijia Shao, Varuna Jayasiri, Nick Haber, Noah D. Goodman (Stanford)
insights: Generalizes STaR: model emits 'thoughts' between every token of the corpus, not just at QA boundaries
Trained with REINFORCE-style estimator on thought-conditioned next-token likelihood — internalizes reasoning
Mistral-7B post-trained with Quiet-STaR improves zero-shot CoT on CommonsenseQA (36.3%→47.2%), GSM8K (5.9%→10.9%)
Predicts and motivates the o1 paradigm: training the model to think internally before responding
Bridges STaR (per-question rationales) and o1 (per-response reasoning) — a key conceptual stepping stone
quotes: We present Quiet-STaR, a generalization of STaR in which LMs learn to generate rationales at each token to explain future text.
After fine-tuning with Quiet-STaR, the LM uses generated thoughts to improve predictions on difficult tokens.

title: RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
author: Chip Huyen
insights: Step-by-step explainer of the 3-stage RLHF pipeline: SFT → reward model → PPO
Walks through math of preference loss (Bradley-Terry) and PPO objective with KL penalty
Identifies real-world pitfalls: reward hacking, mode collapse, KL drift, distribution shift in comparison data
Why RLHF works framing: SFT teaches surface form, RM captures preferences SFT can't express directly
Used widely as the canonical practitioner intro to RLHF before Nathan Lambert's book
quotes: RLHF, short for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, is the technique behind the success of ChatGPT.
The RLHF pipeline can be summarized into three phases: supervised finetuning, reward modeling, and reinforcement learning.

title: Building Reliable LLM-Evaluators: Best Practices
author: Eugene Yan
insights: Concrete playbook for building LLM-as-judge: rubric design, demo curation, format constraints, sanity checks
Prefer binary or low-cardinality scales over Likert — easier to calibrate, less noise
Pre-define what 'good' looks like via labeled examples before writing the judge prompt
Independent of judge model: don't use the model under test as the judge — bake separation in by default
Pairs well with eugeneyan.com/writing/llm-evaluators (the diagnostics/biases post) — design + diagnose
quotes: Build evaluators that reliably measure what you care about.
Pre-define what 'good' looks like via labeled examples before writing the judge prompt.

title: How to Work and Compound with AI
author: Eugene Yan
insights: Practical workflow for working alongside AI tools: amplify drafting, narrow review, iterate fast
Distinguishes 'AI for first draft' from 'AI for final draft' — drastically different review burden
Investment in personal eval infrastructure compounds: reusable judges, repeatable benchmarks
Author's own data points on coding throughput, document creation, research synthesis with AI
Useful for practitioners thinking about how to build LLM-augmented workflows for themselves and teams
quotes: AI is a force multiplier when paired with structured human review.
Investment in personal evaluation infrastructure compounds over time.

title: On the Measure of Intelligence
author: François Chollet
insights: Defines intelligence as 'skill-acquisition efficiency' rather than skill itself — pushes back on benchmarks that test pre-trained skills
Operationalizes generality as a function of priors + experience + breadth of tasks
Introduces ARC as the empirical companion to the theoretical framework
Pre-empted the 'memorization vs reasoning' debate that 2024-2025 reasoning models forced into the mainstream
Required reading for anyone arguing about AGI, scaling, or evaluation methodology
quotes: I argue that the issue of evaluating intelligence has gone unaddressed for a long time, holding back our progress.
Intelligence is the efficiency of skill-acquisition on unknown tasks.

title: Real-world engineering challenges: building Cursor
author: Gergely Orosz (Pragmatic Engineer) + Cursor team
insights: Cursor is a VS Code fork (not extension): editor-level access enables speculative tab completion, Shadow Workspace, background agents
Speculative edits: pushes a 70B model to ~1,000 tokens/sec by using existing source as draft tokens — 13x speedup
Custom sparse code-completion model with RL loop retrained every ~90 minutes against accept/reject signal
Backend at scale: 1M+ TPS at peak, billions of completions/day, end-to-end encrypted snippet routing
Cursor 2.0 introduces multi-agent architecture + proprietary Composer model for in-house agentic editing
quotes: Cursor was a direct fork of VS Code's open-source codebase.
Every AI feature in Cursor, from speculative tab completions to the Shadow Workspace to Background Agents, required editor-level access that no plugin API provides.

title: Aider: AI pair programming in your terminal
author: Paul Gauthier
insights: Terminal-native AI pair programmer: opens edit sessions over real git repos, commits with descriptive messages
Repo-map: builds compact symbol map of entire codebase to feed as context — handles large repos
Model-agnostic: works with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5/4 Sonnet, OSS models via OpenAI-compatible APIs
Strong on its own benchmarks: Aider Polyglot Eval is now a reference for coding model comparisons
Used as 'minimal Aider-style' workflow inspiration in many derivative tools (Continue, OpenHands, plandex)
quotes: Aider lets you pair program with LLMs, to edit code in your local git repository.
Aider makes a map of your entire codebase, which helps it work well in larger projects.

title: How Good Are the Latest Open LLMs? And Is DPO Better Than PPO?
author: Sebastian Raschka
insights: Survey of open LLMs at the time (Llama 3, Phi-3, Mixtral, Qwen) — capability and licensing comparison
Direct comparison of DPO vs PPO across reproducible setups — DPO often matches or beats PPO at lower training cost
Practical recommendation: for most teams, DPO is the better default unless you have specialized PPO infra
Includes from-scratch DPO code in companion repo — practitioner-grade demystification
Companion to broader Ahead of AI coverage of post-training research
quotes: Given that DPO is more straightforward to use and implement, it is expected to remain a popular go-to method.
According to benchmarks, it's more efficient to use DPO and often also preferred over RLHF/PPO in terms of response quality.

title: New LLM Pre-training and Post-training Paradigms
author: Sebastian Raschka
insights: Surveys the evolving recipes in 2024 open frontier models: Llama 3, Qwen-2, Mistral, Phi-3, AI2 OLMoE
Trends in pretraining: more data, more synthetic, higher-quality curation; multi-modal increasingly built-in
Trends in post-training: rejection-sampling SFT, iterative DPO, reasoning RL — replacing pure-PPO RLHF
Compares specifics across labs — same primitives, very different choices in data mix, ablation strategy
Reference resource for engineers wanting to understand what each frontier lab does differently
quotes: This year, we've witnessed remarkable advancements in LLM training methodologies, both during pre-training and post-training stages.
Many recent open LLMs are now trained with a recipe of rejection-sampling SFT followed by multiple rounds of DPO.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
author: OpenAI
insights: GPT-4 launch paper: Transformer-based next-token model, multi-modal (text + image input), large capability lift vs GPT-3.5
Reports professional/academic exam performance (bar exam top 10%, AMC 10/12 high scores) — emergent expert-level competence
Includes detailed system card on bias, disinformation, over-reliance, cybersecurity, proliferation risks
Predictive scaling: capabilities forecast 1000x smaller compute — first explicit demonstration of scaling-law-driven deployment
Does NOT disclose architecture, dataset, training compute — set precedent for closed frontier model technical reports
quotes: GPT-4 is a Transformer-based model pre-trained to predict the next token in a document.
The post-training alignment process results in improved performance on measures of factuality and adherence to desired behavior.

title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context
author: Gemini Team, Google DeepMind
insights: First production model with 1M-token context (10M experimental) — qualitative jump in long-doc/video/audio capability
Sparse MoE Transformer architecture — efficiency unlock that made long-context economically viable
Near-perfect needle-in-haystack recall across text, video, audio modalities at million-token scale
Demonstrated novel use cases: full-codebase Q&A, hour-long video understanding, language acquisition from grammar book
Forced industry-wide upgrades: every frontier model since aims for 1M+ context, recalibrating RAG vs. long-context tradeoffs
quotes: The Gemini 1.5 family of models represents the next generation of highly compute-efficient multimodal models capable of recalling and reasoning over fine-grained information from millions of tokens of context.
Gemini 1.5 models achieve near-perfect recall on long-context retrieval tasks across modalities.

title: DSPy MIPROv2 Optimizer
author: Stanford DSPy team
insights: MIPROv2 = Multiprompt Instruction PRoposal Optimizer v2 — current SOTA optimizer in DSPy
Three-phase: bootstrap few-shot demos → propose grounded instructions → Bayesian optimization over (instruction, demo) combinations
Optimizes instructions + demonstrations *jointly* — beats demo-only or instruction-only optimization
Recommended for runs with 200+ training examples; smaller datasets use BootstrapFewShot or COPRO
Production-ready: used by DSPy applications and reference for prompt-optimization research
quotes: MIPROv2 is the new state-of-the-art optimizer for LM programs in DSPy that is even faster, cheaper, and more accurate than MIPRO.
Generates instructions and few-shot examples in each step, with instruction generation that is data-aware and demonstration-aware.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG)
author: Shi-Qi Yan, Jia-Chen Gu, Yun Zhu, Zhen-Hua Ling
insights: Lightweight retrieval evaluator classifies retrieved docs into Correct / Incorrect / Ambiguous — triggers different actions per class
Incorrect retrievals trigger web-search fallback to augment with fresh external information
Decompose-then-recompose algorithm filters retrieved docs to keep only key fragments — improves signal-to-noise
Plug-and-play with any base RAG pipeline; consistent improvements on short and long-form QA
Influential RAG variant (along with Self-RAG, RAFT, HippoRAG) — established the 'evaluative RAG' family
quotes: CRAG improves the robustness of generation in retrieval-augmented systems by introducing a lightweight retrieval evaluator.
A decompose-then-recompose algorithm is designed for retrieved documents to selectively focus on key information and filter out irrelevant information.

title: Context Engineering for Agents
author: LangChain
insights: Frames 'context engineering' as the discipline of curating what enters the model's context window at each step
Four design levers: write (scratchpad), select (RAG/retrieval), compress (summarize), isolate (subagents)
Argues context engineering is the dominant lever after model selection — bigger lift than prompt phrasing
Concrete patterns: long-term memory, episodic summaries, working memory in state, file artifacts
Pairs with 'cognitive architecture' framing: cog arch + context engineering = the application-defining layer
quotes: Context engineering is the discipline of curating what enters the model's context window at each step.
Four key strategies: write, select, compress, and isolate context.

title: OpenAI o1 System Card
author: OpenAI
insights: First reasoning-model system card: details safety evaluations, deceptive reasoning detection, chain-of-thought monitoring
Reports red-team findings: model occasionally generates deceptive plans in CoT, flagged via internal monitor
Capability evaluations on math (AIME, MATH), coding (Codeforces), science (GPQA-Diamond) — establishes the o1 baseline
Discusses 'CoT faithfulness' — extent to which visible CoT corresponds to actual computation
Influences subsequent reasoning model evaluations (DeepSeek-R1, Claude extended thinking, Gemini deep think)
quotes: The o1 model series is trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to reason using chain of thought.
Integrating safety policies into the chain of thought of a reasoning model is an effective way to teach human values.

title: LLM OS (Karpathy thread)
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: LLM-OS analogy: GPT-4 Turbo as 256-core processor @ 20Hz (tok/s), 128K context as RAM, Ada002 embeddings as filesystem
Maps every classical OS primitive to an LLM-era counterpart: agents=long-running apps, tools=syscalls, context=RAM
Predicts ecosystem stratification analogous to Windows/macOS/Linux → GPT/Claude/Llama
Framing widely adopted in 2024-2025: 'agent runtime', 'context budget', 'tool surface' all derived from this lens
Influenced subsequent architectures: MemGPT explicitly OS-inspired, Anthropic Skills, OpenAI's Agents SDK
quotes: LLM OS. Bear with me I'm still cooking.
Specs: LLM: OpenAI GPT-4 Turbo 256 core (batch size) processor @ 20Hz (tok/s) - RAM: 128Ktok - Filesystem: Ada002

title: LLM as OS kernel (Karpathy original thread)
author: Andrej Karpathy
insights: Initial articulation of 'LLM as kernel process of a new OS': orchestrates I/O across modalities, code interpreter, browsing, memory
Frames LLMs as 'in the middle' of capabilities, not the only capability — agents and tools are first-class citizens
Foreshadows the agentic era explicitly months before AutoGPT-style hype peaked
Continues into the dev role evolution: programmers as Software 2.0/3.0 curators rather than direct authors
Cited by virtually every LLM-OS framing — including HuggingFace blog 'Illustrated LLM OS'
quotes: With many puzzle pieces dropping recently, a more complete picture is emerging of LLMs not as a chatbot, but the kernel process of a new Operating System.

title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)
author: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
insights: 57-subject multi-choice benchmark spanning math, history, law, CS, medicine, ethics, etc. — broadest LLM knowledge eval at release
15,908 questions; high human accuracy (~89%) vs initial models near random — became the standard scale of capability
First widely-adopted benchmark to expose emergent capability cliffs at GPT-3 scale
Now nearly saturated by frontier models (~90%+) — MMLU-Pro proposed to extend headroom
Cited in nearly every frontier model release paper as the canonical knowledge-and-reasoning yardstick
quotes: We propose a new test to measure a text model's multitask accuracy. The test covers 57 tasks including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science, law, and more.
To attain high accuracy on this test, models must possess extensive world knowledge and problem solving ability.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (Codex, HumanEval)
author: Mark Chen, Jerry Tworek, Heewoo Jun, Qiming Yuan, Henrique Ponde de Oliveira Pinto, Jared Kaplan, Harrison Edwards, Yuri Burda, Nicholas Joseph, Greg Brockman et al. (OpenAI)
insights: Codex: GPT-3 fine-tuned on GitHub code — basis of GitHub Copilot, first widely deployed code LLM
HumanEval benchmark: 164 hand-written Python problems with unit tests — measures functional correctness
pass@1 vs pass@k metrics: repeated sampling lifts 28.8% → 70.2% with 100 samples per problem
Codex-S finetuned on standalone correct functions: 37.7% pass@1 — early demonstration of specialization wins
Foundational paper for the entire LLM coding agenda; HumanEval remains the gold-standard short coding benchmark
quotes: Codex is a GPT language model fine-tuned on publicly available code from GitHub.

On HumanEval, a new evaluation set we release to measure functional correctness for synthesizing programs from docstrings, our model solves 28.8% of the problems, while GPT-3 solves 0% and GPT-J solves 11.4%.

title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (GSM8K)
author: Karl Cobbe, Vineet Kosaraju, Mohammad Bavarian, Mark Chen, Heewoo Jun, Lukasz Kaiser, Matthias Plappert, Jerry Tworek, Jacob Hilton, Reiichiro Nakano, Christopher Hesse, John Schulman (OpenAI)
insights: Introduces GSM8K: 8.5K human-written grade-school math word problems with step-by-step solutions
Verifier method: generate many candidate solutions → train a verifier to score correctness → pick highest-scored
Verifier-based selection scales better with sampling than picking by model probability
Pre-cursor to PRM line (Let's Verify Step by Step) and the broader reasoning-RL agenda
GSM8K remains the standard sanity-check for arithmetic reasoning in every frontier model evaluation
quotes: GSM8K consists of 8.5K high quality grade school math problems created by human problem writers, segmented into 7.5K training problems and 1K test problems.
We propose training verifiers to judge the correctness of model completions.

title: Understanding Reasoning LLMs
author: Sebastian Raschka
insights: Four approaches to building reasoning models: prompt-based (CoT/ToT), search-based (verifier/MCTS), RL-based (GRPO), distillation from reasoning teacher
Defines reasoning narrowly: multi-step problems with intermediate computation — not all hard problems are reasoning problems
Recommends reasoning models specifically for puzzles, math proofs, advanced coding — not for summarization or factual QA
Reviews DeepSeek-R1 recipe in detail: cold-start → RL → reject-sample → final SFT → final RL
Pairs with companion 'Reasoning From Scratch' book — accessible technical depth for engineers
quotes: Reasoning, in the LLM context, can be broadly viewed as inference-time scaling.

Reasoning models are designed to be good at complex tasks such as solving puzzles, advanced math problems, and challenging coding tasks. However, they are not necessary for simpler tasks like summarization, translation, or knowledge-based question answering.

title: Function Calling (Mistral docs)
author: Mistral AI
insights: Mistral function-calling spec: JSON Schema for tools, tool_choice control, parallel tool calls supported
Four-step pattern: user → model emits tool call → app executes → result fed back to model
Mistral Large 2 and Codestral support native function calling — comparable to GPT-4/Claude in OpenAI-compatible mode
Cookbook covers local function calling with Mistral 7B + Ollama — open-stack reproducibility
Companion to OpenAI/Anthropic tool-use docs; Mistral's contribution is strong support in OSS models
quotes: Function calling allows Mistral models to connect to external local tools.
